The Eliste Gallery is one of the landmarks of Laerta. Marble statues of the mirnas stand on its roof, turning pink at sunset: this is the very image that opens Alvaro’s evening walk in the preface.

The collection

The gallery is famous for its three-hundred-year-old collection: faded icons from the previous millennium, resembling children’s drawings with patches of gilding; battle panoramas from the feudal era (“The Battle of Lamertina,” “The Conquest of Brega,” “The Death of King Augustus the Pale”); portraits by Velanyes, with stiff poses but lifelike faces; and engravings by Emil Flare. Scandalous works are shown on the temporary-exhibitions floor.

The “Philosophy of Horror” exhibition (ch. 16, 18)

In chapter 16, the gallery hosts “Philosophy of Horror: An Artist’s View of the Myths of the Ancients.” Don Filippe invites Alvaro and takes him from canvas to canvas: Iolanta and Alessina argue about art, Darreggio inserts a small steam engine into his belly, Ikhtrodan the Shipbreaker is coiled into a ring like a serpent, and the mirna of luck, Eliga, is shown with a bullet hole in her temple. The exhibition shares its title with van Halm’s unfinished book (Philosophy of Horror). According to the characters, four days before chapter 18, Doña Isabel disappeared near the gallery during this exhibition.
